conventions.convention: Framework stability models use open configuration domains in R^(3N), fixed positive masses, and continuous force maps locally Lipschitz in state, locally uniformly in time. Proper open restrictions have their own maximal lifetimes. Autonomous models have time window R; periodic restriction domains are preserved by integer shifts of the forcing period.

Lyapunov stability quantifies over maximal solutions, requires forward completeness for sufficiently close data, and does not include attraction. Linear stability means bounded forward solutions of the variational equation. Hyperbolicity excludes complex eigenvalues with zero real part for fields, or modulus one for maps.

Finite-time tangent rates use the Euclidean norm of numerical state coordinates and positive times. A Lyapunov exponent is assigned only for forward-unbounded lifetime and an existing finite real limit; infinite values are not assigned.

Stroboscopic maps are partial maps requiring the restricted maximal motion to exist throughout a full period. A local Poincare return branch uses positive crossing time; its first-return interpretation additionally requires exclusion of intervening hits from the section closure.

Chaos means continuity, topological mixing, dense periodic points, and sensitivity with a positive uniform constant, on a stated nonempty invariant domain with its restricted Euclidean metric. Positive tangent growth alone is not this predicate.

Rotor angles are radian angles modulo 2π. The canonical form is Σ dθ_i ∧ dΠ_i, with Hamilton equations θ'=H_Π and Π'=-H_θ. Dimensionless momenta and time use J0=√(I E0) and t0=√(I/E0); physical angular frequencies are ω0ν_i. Countable Choice is assumed.

The physical horseshoe uses Newtonian position-velocity coordinates, axial momentum Π=m v_Q, and physical forcing period (π/2+δ)/ω0. Countable and Dependent Choice are assumed. Coded position and momentum bounds apply at stroboscopic times.

Recurrence concerns Borel subsets of a bounded invariant Borel phase set whose closure lies inside the phase domain, with complete flow on that set. Returns are at positive integer multiples of the declared time unit, almost everywhere in phase Lebesgue measure. Countable Choice is assumed.

load_bearing.statement: Defines stability models, restricted maximal motions, autonomous local flows, equilibria, nonconstant complete periodic motions, and invariant sets. For an autonomous model, invariance requires existence for every real time and Φ_t(S)=S for every real t.

Defines Lyapunov, asymptotic, orbital and linear stability, and hyperbolicity, for the separately declared framework force models and mechanical chart models; map predicates concern the derivative of a C1 branch at a fixed point.

For n≥1, an open configuration chart, a C2 symmetric positive-definite kinetic metric M, a C2 potential U and a critical point q0: a strict local minimum is Lyapunov stable; a negative Hessian eigenvalue gives linear instability; a negative-definite Hessian gives nonlinear instability; exact energy conservation excludes asymptotic stability when states of different energy accumulate at (q0,0).

For the declared C2 mechanical chart data and a ball satisfying 0<ρ<R-M_R T, the flow derivative solves the variational equation and nearby solutions obey the exponential Lipschitz bound. For constant M, Mη''=-D²U(q(t))η. At an equilibrium, declared quadratic-remainder and linear-growth bounds with δe^(LT)<r yield the displayed finite-time linearization error bound.

A self-map of a nonempty metric space is chaotic in the stated sense exactly when it is continuous, topologically mixing, has dense periodic points, and has sensitive dependence with a positive constant.

Assuming Countable and Dependent Choice, for the explicitly adopted smooth one-label Cartesian force model with a≥100 there is δ0>0 depending only on a and the bump such that every 0<δ<δ0 gives a compact coded invariant set conjugate to the bilateral two-sign shift, chaotic in the stated sense, with two full-phase hyperbolic fixed points and transverse homoclinic points for nonconstant codes with identical constant tails.

Assuming Countable Choice, for the adopted equal-inertia two-rotor Hamiltonian and every τ>1 there is c>0 determined by the fixed dimensionless analytic data such that 0<α<c and 0<ε≤cα² give a positive-measure Diophantine label set in C* and an invariant C1 Lagrangian embedded torus for each label, carrying physical angular frequencies ω0ν_i.

Assuming Countable Choice, for the adopted autonomous potential presentation and a bounded invariant Borel phase set A with closure inside the phase domain and flow defined on A for every real time, phase volume is finite and preserved on its Borel subsets; for every Borel E⊆A, almost every x∈E returns to E at infinitely many positive integer times.

concerns.concern: Definition (ii) says the time-P map is restricted to Ω_P={(P,z):(P,z)∈Ω}. This is a set of time-state pairs, whereas Φ_P takes states as inputs. The cited local-flow definition instead has Ω_P={z:(P,z)∈Ω}. The written domain is ill-typed, although the intended correction is evident.

Statement (i) and step 1.1 call the whole plane P={Y=Z=v_Y=v_Z=0} 'invariant'. The earlier invariant-set definition is for autonomous models and includes completeness for every point. This model is nonautonomous, and the supplier supplies full-period existence only near the coding box, not completeness on the entire polynomial axial plane. Define the intended preservation while solutions exist; the compact coded set's completeness is separately established in step 4.1.

The title and physical_scope say 'the fixed points are 1 plus or minus sqrt(101)' without the limiting-map qualification. The Example correctly defines r± as fixed points of the limiting quadratic map, and step 2.1 computes only those points. The positive-width physical period map has perturbed fixed points supplied by the horseshoe theorem, not these exact coordinates. Carry the existing qualification into the title and public scope.

The first Remark describes 'a single negative Hessian eigenvalue together with positive ... eigenvalues' and then gives rates ±sqrt(-λ_j) and ±i sqrt(λ_k). These formulas require λ_i to denote eigenvalues of S=M0^(-1/2) K M0^(-1/2), as in proof step 1.2, rather than eigenvalues of K. Make that distinction explicit: for M0=4 and K=1 the rate is ±i/2, not ±i. The main proof uses the correct normalized matrix.

Fact L3 attributes openness of the entire maximal-flow domain and C1 regularity there to thm-cm-smooth-dependence-and-the-variational-equation. Its Statement gives regularity only on a quantitative ball/time cylinder. The exact global-domain conclusion is in cor-cm-flow-domain-open-and-flow-is-c1, already used elsewhere in this batch. Cite that corollary or explicitly give the finite continuation argument.

The Statement permits A=∅. Step 1.1 then takes a finite cover of K=closure(A) and sets h=min_i h_i, without arranging a nonempty index family. For the empty set, a zero-member cover has no such minimum. The conclusion is vacuous; separate that case before the cover construction.

The title promises 'linear stability of equilibria and periodic orbits'. The Definition gives equilibrium and map-fixed-point predicates, but does not explicitly define linear stability of a continuous-time periodic orbit through a variational or return-map convention. Either supply that promised convention or align the title with the actual definitions.

alerts.finding: Definition (a) defines D=I0×Q×R^(3N), a time-state domain. Definition (c) then writes 'the state curve z=(x, xdot):J→D' and repeatedly requires 'z(t)∈D'. The pair z(t)=(x(t),xdot(t)) has only state coordinates and cannot belong to that time-state domain. The correct graph condition is (t,z(t))∈D, with z:J→Q×R^(3N). Definition (e) already uses the correctly typed state codomain. This is an explicit type mismatch in the supplier's motion equivalence.
